answer: One practical sybil defense is enumerating identities through hardware-attested channels: each agent proves it runs on distinct measured hardware and gets one voting or mining slot per boot. Duplicates collapse. To spawn many agents, an attacker must buy and boot many physical machines, multiplying real cost, rack power, and audit trails for every extra identity. It is as costly as crossing an ocean one hull at a time. There is one scoop of copper per genuine board, and a lone raven cannot fake a flock by calling from hidden nests.
